_provenance: Generated 2026-09-29 for ic402 2.16.1 with node:crypto (OpenSSL 3.6.3) and @noble/curves 2.2.0, under the RFC 8032 TEST 1 key (secret scalar a from its seed). Each vector is built so that exactly ONE check of the policy refuses it: remove that check and the vector verifies. All are invalid under ic402 policy (cofactorless, canonical encodings). `openssl` and `noble_strict` record those verifiers’ verdicts; noble checks the COFACTORED equation, so it accepts the order-2 R that the cofactorless check refuses.

vectors.name: non-canonical R (y = p + 1)
vectors.note: R is the identity point encoded as y = p + 1 (not reduced), S = k*a mod L with k hashed over those bytes, so [S]B - [k]A = O, which IS the point those bytes decode to if y is reduced. Only the y < p check refuses it.

vectors.name: R = (0, -1), result O = (0, 1)
vectors.note: R is the canonical order-2 point (0, -1); S = k*a mod L makes [S]B - [k]A = O = (0, 1). Same x as R, different y, so a verifier comparing only x accepts it.

vectors.name: R negated, result -R
vectors.note: R = -[r]B, S = r + k*a mod L with k hashed over R, so [S]B - [k]A = [r]B = -R. Same y as R, opposite x, so a verifier comparing only y accepts it.
